subject: Private deployment: terms flexing & on-call / SLA options
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@medtech.co>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jill Harper <jill.harper@medtech.co>
Date: Sat, 28 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment cost and on-call arrangement - MedTech / Redwood

Rafael,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated VPC path looks promising for our regulated workloads. Procurement asked me to follow up with more specificity on three items before we request an internal budget: 1) platform fee treatment (we need predictability on the platform/management fee that’s billed on top of reserved capacity), 2) support / on-call options for 24/7 incident response, and 3) any migration or uplift credits you can offer to offset initial engineering costs.

Our constraints: we can commit to a 12-month reserved capacity baseline if the economics make sense, but our procurement requires a minimal platform fee in year 1 and a clear SLO/penalty for critical incidents. Can you share a concrete package we can take to finance (ballpark numbers are fine) and a draft SOW we can circulate to legal? Also please flag any items that would block us from getting an accelerated pilot in April.

Appreciate it,
Sandeep

--
Sandeep Rao
Director of Cloud Ops, MedTech Health Systems
S: (415) 555-0113
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@medtech.co>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment cost and on-call arrangement - MedTech / Redwood

Hi Sandeep — thanks for the clear ask. I put together two pragmatic options so Procurement has something to evaluate quickly; I’ve attached a short pricing summary and a draft SOW. High-level:

Option A — Pilot-friendly (12-month commit)
- Reserved capacity commit (12 months) with metered overage
- Platform fee: waived for first 3 months, then 40% of standard platform fee for remainder of year 1
- Support: Premier Lite — business-hours coverage + 2 emergency on-call escalations / quarter included; paid 24/7 on-call at an hourly reduced rate after that (details in attached PDF)
- Migration credit: $25k one-time credit applied to first invoice if you sign SOW by Apr 30

Option B — Enterprise-ready (12+ month commit, 24/7 SLOs)
- Reserved capacity higher minimum (guaranteed throughput slotting)
- Platform fee: 50% discount in year 1 if you accept Premier (24/7) support
- Support: Premier — 24/7 on-call with guaranteed response times (P1: 30 min, P2: 4 hours), 4 emergency callbacks / quarter included. Reduced hourly rates for after-hours engineering at committed rates
- Audit & retention: standard 90-day access logs included; extended retention available as add-on

Note on SLAs: we can include service credits for missed P1 response times but we need to cap exposure; standard proposal limits credits to a percentage of monthly platform fee (I’ve proposed 25% monthly cap in the attached SOW).

Next steps I suggest:
- Laura (cc) will follow up with a pricing spreadsheet we can redline for Procurement
- If you like Option A we can start a pilot immediately and lock in the migration credit; Option B will need a short exec review for the deeper discount.

Laura — any constraints from finance on the concessions above?

Sandeep — attaching: Redwood_Private_Pricing_20260328.pdf and SOW_draft_MED-47_v3.docx. I can join a quick procurement call this week.

Best,
Rafael

--
Rafael Mendes
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
T: (650) 555-0199
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment cost and on-call arrangement - MedTech / Redwood

Raf — quick internal redline from Sales/Finance POV:

- Platform fee concession: OK to waive first 3 months for a 12-month commitment, but Finance is wary of a full 50% year-1 discount unless we lock a minimum guaranteed GPU-hours SKU (suggested floor: 320 reserved GPU-hours / month). Recommend counter in Option B: 50% off platform fee if they commit to the floor and a 12-month prepay or ACH cadence.

- On-call / SLA mechanics: We should limit included emergency callbacks to 4 / quarter for Premier and 2 / quarter for Premier Lite; after that use a scaled incident fee. For P1 credits, Finance wants a stated cap (25% monthly cap is fine) and a single-incident credit max. Also recommend defining "critical incident" narrowly (security incident or service unavailability impacting >50% of provisioned capacity).

- Professional services / migration credits: $25k credit OK but tie to execution milestones (kickoff + data ingress completion). Also insist on an exit data-handling clause (48-72 hours transfer window + temporary egress support at cost).

- Audit log retention: extending beyond 90 days should be charged; ask Legal to confirm compliance filtering for PHI logs before we commit to extended retention.

Steph — can you run numbers for the 320 GPU-hours floor + 50% discount scenario and confirm gross margin?

If MedTech signs SOW by Apr 30 we can lock the migration credit; otherwise keep the pilot-friendly waiver but remove migration credit.

Ben

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Director, Redwood Inference
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@medtech.co>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jill Harper <jill.harper@medtech.co>, procurement@medtech.co
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment cost and on-call arrangement - MedTech / Redwood

Rafael / team — thanks for the clear options and quick turnaround. Procurement likes Option A for the faster pilot but Procurement and Finance are pushing for a clearer path to Option B if the pilot satisfies throughput tests. Two clarifications before we proceed: 1) confirm the exact definition of "GPU-hours" you referenced (does it include reserved headroom for burst?), and 2) please confirm the DocuSign link for the SOW so Procurement can start routing (we’re on a tight April PO cadence).

We’re comfortable with the milestone tie on the migration credit. If you can confirm the 3-month waiver + $25k credit in DocuSign and include the Pilot acceptance criteria in the SOW (throughput target + acceptable latency percentile), we’ll route to legal and aim to have a PO by mid-April.

Please send DocuSign and I'll loop procurement.

Thanks,
Sandeep

--
Sandeep Rao
Director of Cloud Ops, MedTech Health Systems
